decisions.reason: As a consumer-facing superfood product furthest from the firm's core industrial technology business, it likely has higher ongoing commercialization costs and lower strategic option value than the firm's other ventures.

These modular waste-to-energy extensions fit the established portfolio and are relatively cheap to keep available as a complementary industrial option while demand in long-cycle projects remains uncertain.

This waste-oil-to-energy plant showed the strongest launch commitment and best fit with the firm's core decentralized sustainability technologies, so its option value likely still exceeds its carrying cost.
A plastic-waste-to-fuel plant is close to the firm's established offer and preserves upside in circular-economy markets, making it worth retaining while commercial uncertainty is still unresolved.
